_provenance.purpose: WS2 T3.2 Step 2 - compositional cardinal-number generation data, shared by faTextNormalize.ts and fa/text.rs
_provenance.status: landed Step 2 (data only) - not yet consumed by either implementation
notes: cardinals0to99 extends the existing FRENCH_CARDINALS_0_30 table verbatim for 0-30 (including the index-21 space-wall exclusion), then continues to 99 - 70-79 are 'soixante' + teens (vigesimal), 90-99 are 'quatre-vingt' + teens, per real French grammar, NOT derived from a generic tens+unit rule.

Six values require the space-linked 'et' connector and are therefore not representable by today's tokenizer: 21, 31, 41, 51, 61, 71 - every other 2-digit value is hyphen-joined and already representable.

'cent' pluralizes to 'cents' ONLY when it is the last element (exact multiple, e.g. 'deux cents'=200) and drops the 's' when a remainder follows ('deux cent trois'=203) - encoded via pluralizesWhenExactMultiple, not two separate word forms.
'mille' (thousand) is orthographically invariant - never takes a plural 's', unlike 'cent'.
Values whose composed reading contains a space are NOT representable by the FA tokenizer today - see scoped-in multi-word tokenizer extension.

knownLossy.gap: pluralizesWhenExactMultiple/pluralSuffix only look at the REMAINDER within composeHundred's own 0-999 block (remainder===0 && multiplier>1) to decide whether 'cent' pluralizes. They have no signal for whether this hundred value is itself about to be used as a scale-level MULTIPLIER for a further NUMERAL scale word ('mille') vs. standing alone or feeding a NOUN scale word ('million'). Real French grammar blocks the plural only in the former case: 'deux cent mille' (200000, no s on cent) but 'deux cents' (200 alone, s stays correct) and 'deux cents millions' (200000000, s stays correct because 'million' is a noun, not a bare numeral). The generator currently pluralizes unconditionally whenever the local remainder is 0, so it produces 'deux cents mille' for 200000, which is wrong.
knownLossy.owningTask: WS2 T3.2 follow-up (unscheduled) - needs a new schema signal (e.g. a suppressPluralBeforeNumeralScaleWord flag on FaHundredConfig) threaded from composeScaleLevel's multiplier-count call into composeHundred so it knows a numeral scale word follows. Deliberately not built in WS2 T3.2 Step 3 (durability pass) or the Step 3b-iii session that first found it (.work-phase4/session-ws2-35/t32-step3b-iii-generator.md, NOT DETERMINED #3) - several orders of magnitude past any digit token measured in any real corpus content to date (WS2 T3.2 Step 2's own margin measurement found nothing past 2-3 digits in v6/173/spanish), and fixing it needs a new schema field on top of an already-large change.

yearReading.note: Standard French has no pair-style year-reading convention - years are read as the full cardinal ('mille neuf cent quatre-vingt-dix-huit'). Single real candidate - flagging for operator confirmation rather than assuming.
